purpose: Metaxalone is used to help relieve pain and discomfort caused by muscle injuries, sprains, or strains. It is usually used along with rest and physical therapy to help your muscles heal. It helps you feel more comfortable so you can move and recover more easily.
how_it_works: Metaxalone works by acting on your brain and nervous system to help reduce muscle spasms and tension. It does not work directly on the muscle itself, but rather calms down the signals in your nervous system that are causing the muscle to tighten up. Think of it like a dimmer switch that turns down the overactive nerve signals causing your pain and stiffness.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include drowsiness, dizziness, headache, nausea, and an upset stomach. Some people may also feel irritable or have trouble with coordination. Because it can make you sleepy, be careful when driving or using machinery.
warnings: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medication, as it can make drowsiness much worse and can be dangerous. Tell your doctor if you have any liver or kidney problems, as this drug may not be safe for you. Avoid taking other medications that cause drowsiness, such as sleep aids or anxiety medications, without checking with your doctor first. Do not take more than prescribed.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 800 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day, as directed by your doctor. It is best taken with food if it upsets your stomach. Try to take it at evenly spaced times throughout the day to keep your symptoms well controlled.
